_comment: Model catalogue v2 (schema 2), read by Android 0.7.0+ and desktop 0.6.0+. Builds before those read models.json (schema 1) and reject any other schema, so both files are kept; desktop/tests/test_shared.py checks that every schema-1 model appears here with the same id, repo and manifest_url. Lines are what a model is trained for (Sabich = everything, Jachnun = code-switching only, Shakshuka = streaming); variants are the same line on another base model. A variant is downloadable in an app only if its engine is in that app's supported engines AND its status is 'available'; other variants are listed greyed with runs_on and a card link. Variant ids are permanent (they name the folder models/<id>/); never reuse or rename one. speed and accuracy are 1-5 tiers, estimates relative to the other Hebrish models, not benchmark results. Protocol: shared/update-protocol.md.

tiers.speed: 1 = slowest, 5 = fastest, each on the hardware it is meant for
tiers.accuracy: 1 = most mistakes, 5 = fewest, on English with Hebrew and tech words in it

lines.name: Sabich
lines.summary: The complete model: English with Hebrew words and tech vocabulary: arnona, Kubernetes, 250 shekels.

variants.name: Sabich
variants.hardware: Phone or computer, no GPU needed; about 1.5 GB of RAM
variants.recommendation: Start here: the best all-round choice on a phone or any recent computer.

variants.name: Sabich-Qwen3-ASR-1.7B
variants.hardware: Desktop with a GPU: 5 GB of VRAM or more (CUDA, ROCm/HIP or Vulkan)
variants.recommendation: The most accurate, for a desktop with a GPU. Not in the Hebrish apps yet.
variants.runs_on: llama.cpp (CUDA, HIP or Vulkan) with the GGUF builds on a desktop GPU; transcribe.cpp in the Offline Voice Input app on Android, slow on phones.

variants.name: Sabich-Parakeet-110M
variants.hardware: Any phone, an older computer, a watch or a wearable; about 0.4 GB of RAM
variants.recommendation: For older phones and wearables: a fifth of the size and faster, with more mistakes.

variants.name: Sabich-asr4all-M
variants.hardware: Wearables and very low-end phones; about 0.3 GB of RAM
variants.recommendation: Tiny, for wearables: live text, writes numbers as words. Not published yet.
variants.runs_on: FUTO's asr4all runtime (ONNX or ExecuTorch), with its punctuation model. Not published yet.

variants.name: Sabich-asr4all-S
variants.hardware: Wearables and very low-end phones; about 0.2 GB of RAM
variants.recommendation: The smallest and fastest, for the weakest devices; writes numbers as words. Not published yet.
variants.runs_on: FUTO's asr4all runtime (ONNX or ExecuTorch), with its punctuation model. Not published yet.

lines.name: Jachnun
lines.summary: English + Hebrew vocabulary, without the tech: teudat zehut, arnona, makolet.

variants.name: Jachnun
variants.hardware: Phone or computer, no GPU needed; about 1.5 GB of RAM
variants.recommendation: Hebrew words without the tech vocabulary. Sabich does all of this and more.

lines.name: Shakshuka
lines.summary: Streaming: the words appear while you speak. Trained on everything Sabich is.

variants.name: Shakshuka
variants.hardware: Phone or computer, no GPU needed; about 1.5 GB of RAM
variants.recommendation: Live text while you talk; a little less accurate than Sabich.
variants.runs_on: sherpa-onnx's streaming recognizer (OnlineRecognizer). The Hebrish apps add it in a later release.

lines.name: Parakeet (stock)
lines.summary: Standard English, without the Hebrew words. NVIDIA's release, unchanged.

variants.name: Parakeet (stock)
variants.hardware: Phone or computer, no GPU needed; about 1.5 GB of RAM
variants.recommendation: Plain English with no Hebrew words, as NVIDIA released it.
